archetype.name: Dual-Threat (developing)
archetype.definition: A second-year starter whose rookie value came as much from designed runs and scrambles as from his arm, and who opened 2026 showing a quicker, more accurate passing game before injury pulled him off the field.

report.headline: Two weeks of real growth, then IR and a slide to QB3
report.take:
Dart's 2026 is a brief, encouraging season on hold. As a rookie he was a legs-first starter: 487 rushing yards (3rd among QBs) covered for a passing line that ranked in the bottom half in completion rate (63.7%), YPA (6.7) and CPOE (about -0.2). The Giants built around that, and they still lean on the run, at -4.8% pass rate over expected (27th).

The opener showed a different passer. Against Dallas he went 23/29 for 230 yards and 3 TDs with +18.4 EPA, and his rates moved the right way across the board. Time to throw fell from 2.82 to 2.64 seconds, bad-throw rate dropped from 15% to 11.8%, and CPOE climbed by 4.2 points while his aggressiveness also rose. That combination matters: he was throwing into tighter windows more often and still completing more. It points to faster processing, not just a softer menu of throws. The production came from the middle of the field. He posted +0.985 EPA per attempt at 10-19 air yards and went 9-of-9 on third-down attempts, all but one converted, with Isaiah Likely the main beneficiary at +1.21 EPA per target.

The headline rates need heavy discounting. Nearly all of the season is that one game, and the Dallas defense now ranks 32nd in EPA. In Week 2 against the Rams (4th) his day ended after 12% of snaps, 3/5 for 20 yards. He didn't practice the following week and is on injured reserve. His 1st-ranked EPA per dropback and TD rate rest on 38 dropbacks, and the red-zone line (7 attempts, 3 TDs, 100% completions) is the kind of number that always regresses. His 0-for-3 on deep throws is too small a sample to mean much either way.

The bigger issue is where he stands, not how he played. Jameis Winston started Weeks 3-6, J.J. McCarthy has started every game since, and the depth chart lists Dart third. No return date is on file for him. Even a healthy return now means winning the job back from McCarthy, so for the rest of 2026 he is a development question more than a weekly one. What stays with him is a promising sign that the accuracy can catch up to the legs.

strengths.title: Middle-of-field timing and accuracy
strengths.body: His best work came on 10-19 yard throws and through the middle, the throws that need anticipation. The faster release and the lower bad-throw rate suggest this is a real step from his rookie year, though it rests on about a dozen attempts against a weak defense.

strengths.title: Designed runs as a real weapon
strengths.body: Ranking 3rd in QB rushing as a rookie showed the legs are part of who he is. In 2026 his six designed runs were all successful at 8.17 yards a carry. That threat pulls defenders down and opens the play-action middle where he did his damage, so it should carry over whenever he plays.

strengths.title: Ball security
strengths.body: He threw no interceptions on 34 attempts, after a rookie year of 5 picks in 12 games. The quicker decisions back it up, but this is the least proven of the three given the volume.

concerns.title: Injured reserve and a lost job
concerns.body: He has been on IR since early in the season, with no return date listed. McCarthy has started the last four games, and Dart sits third on the depth chart. That is the main driver of his outlook, more than any part of his play.

concerns.title: The hot start came against the worst defense
concerns.body: Almost all of his 2026 EPA came in the opener against a Dallas defense now ranked 32nd. His brief Week 2 against the 4th-ranked Rams was negative. The improvement in mechanics looks real, but the efficiency ranks are a one-game sample.

concerns.title: Sacks once he's pressured
concerns.body: A third of his pressures became sacks, which ranked 30th of 45. As a rookie the rate was 36.5% (43rd), so this is a lasting trait. It is the cost of a runner who tries to extend plays, but his 2026 scrambles added almost nothing, so the trade isn't paying off yet.

trend.note: He was excellent in Week 1 against Dallas, then left Week 2 at the Rams after 12% of snaps and has not played since. His slide is about availability and standing on the depth chart, not a decline in how he played.

nextGame.headline: On IR as QB3; a soft Colts secondary waits for someone else
nextGame.body:
On paper this matchup suits his game. Indianapolis ranks 29th in explosive pass rate allowed and 23rd on short passes. It gives up the most production to lead backs and a lot to tight ends (27th in EPA allowed to TE1), which fits a passer whose best target was Likely and who works the middle of the field. The Giants are 6.5-point favorites with a 41.5 total against a Colts offense ranked 32nd in pass EPA. That suggests a game the Giants control, with the run game leading.

None of it is likely to be his. He is on injured reserve and listed third behind McCarthy, who has started four straight. On the other side the Colts are missing both outside corners, Charvarius Ward and Sauce Gardner, along with both starting tackles. That helps whichever Giants QB plays and the Giants' pass rush, which ranks 27th in hit rate. Tyrone Tracy's possible return from IR is slated for Week 13, not this game.

keyMatchups.title: Colts without both starting corners
keyMatchups.body: Ward and Gardner, each on 87% of snaps, are out, and the Colts already allow explosive passes at a bottom-four rate. Whoever starts for New York should find open outside throws. That doesn't help Dart unless he's activated.

keyMatchups.title: Tight ends against Indianapolis
keyMatchups.body: The Colts allow 0.42 EPA per target to lead tight ends, 27th in the league. Likely was Dart's most productive target. That pairing is exactly what made his Week 1 work.

keyMatchups.title: Favored game script, run-first offense
keyMatchups.body: Big favorites with a run lean and a lead-back matchup ranked 32nd point to a ground-heavy plan. Even an active QB would likely see modest attempts.

nextGame.watch: Whether Dart is designated to return from IR or moves up the depth chart; without either, he doesn't play.

restOfSeason.body:
The likeliest path is little or no 2026 action. He is on IR with no return date on file and behind two healthy starters, McCarthy and Winston. If he returns and wins the job back, expect something between his rookie self and his Week 1. The quicker release and better accuracy look like real growth. The legs remain a steady floor. The 76.5% completion rate, the red-zone perfection and the top-ranked EPA per dropback will come down toward last year's middle-of-the-pack passing marks.

The ranges below describe a full start, not his expected weekly output, and the chance he starts again this season looks small. In a run-leaning offense, think roughly 170-220 passing yards and 25-45 rushing yards when he plays, about one passing TD a game, with an occasional interception returning.
swingFactors: Whether the Week 1 accuracy gains carry against average defenses

confidence.note: 38 dropbacks, mostly one game against the league's worst defense, now on IR as QB3
